chapter: Paris, Lester Young, drugs, Mississippi and later sessions
title: Working with Sinatra: no recordings, Al Viola, his musicians and politics
summary: He never recorded with Sinatra but filled in for Al Viola, praised the musicians he carried and the stool duet, and disliked his later politics.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: We also talked about the -- Frank Sinatra, and I know you worked with him in live performance.
Have you ever recorded with Frank?

No, I never recorded with Frank. I only did -- well, you know, I worked with him in Vegas quite a bit, and I did some tours with him, you know, but I just never recorded with him. Actually Al Viola was his guitarist, Al has been recording with him and working with him for years and years. But I would replace Al when Al couldn't make it or something, I would replace him. And it was quite a pleasure working with Frank because he's got that charisma, and he is quite a musician also. You know, he's just a perfectionist and it's a pleasure, it was a pleasure to be associated with him, to work with him. Because he carried the best musicians with him too, and so it was a pleasure working with them.

You know, he carried his own key men. Of course Bill Miller, as I mentioned, was playing piano for Red Norro and Mildred Bailey when I first met him in the thirties. He's been Frank's conductor for quite a few years, and Pete Condola was the first trumpet player, and the drummer -- Irv Cotler.

Irv Cotler, and he had two violinists, Raderman, Mrs. Raderman, I can't think of their -- Sally Raderman and Lou Raderman. And he didn't have a bass with us, we would pick up a bass when we -- when I was with him, and myself. And I would always -- he's alway featuring me, and I would always do a number with him. I would take --
we would get the stool and we would do the bit together, and that was a thrill because I just loved playing for him, you know.
Didn't like his politics, of course, but --
You mean his latter day politics.
His earlier politics were all right
Yeah, they were all right, but, you know, he's like a chameleon, he just changes colors on those politics, you know.
